The data from the [2023 TomTom Traffic Index](https://www.tomtom.com/traffic-index/ranking/?country=US) has officially been shared and according to the insights it’s collected over the past year, Washington, D.C. has the second-worst traffic in the United States! The rating may come as little to no shocker to us Washingtonians who have been dealing with DMV area drivers all our lives ([looking at you MD drivers](https://secretdc.com/maryland-virginia-drivers/), sorry not sorry), but it’s nice to be vindicated by real data and see how our cities traffic compares to other cities in the United States.

# Washington, D.C. Traffic Is Officially The Second Worst Traffic In The Country
## How bad is D.C. traffic?
According to the 2023 TomTom Traffic Index, D.C. traffic is among the slowest in the entire country, ranking at **#2 in the U.S.**behind only NYC. D.C. traffic was rated the **5th worst in all of North America**, and the overall **55th worst in the entire world**. The average travel time per 10 km (equal to just over 6 miles) in D.C. this past year was measured at **21 minutes and 20 seconds**, which happens to be a 10-second increase from the average in 2022. Given how slow it takes to get from place to place in the city, it seems fitting that the average speed during rush hour in D.C. was**14 mph**, which is painfully slow for those trying to get to their destinations on time.
![Image 7: d.c. traffic](https://offloadmedia.feverup.com/secretdc.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/19085624/dc-traffic-2.jpg)
Image via f11photo from Getty Images
To convert the reality of how bad D.C. traffic was in 2023, the**average Washingtonian lost about 86 hours of their time last year just sitting in D.C. traffic** during rush hour. In other words, even if you spent three days straight sitting in your car without ever leaving, you’d still have 14 additional hours to equate to the amount of time that the average D.C. driver spent sitting around in traffic last year!
Additionally, based on the calculations of the Traffic Index, this past year the average one-way commute in D.C. of around 6 miles would result in a yearly total of 205 hours spent driving, over 2,000 lbs of CO2 emissions, and around $418 spent on gas. The most shocking aspect of that average is that it’s also only considering a one-way commute, and considering how commutes are certainly a two-way obligation, you can assume the averages above can be roughly doubled for D.C. drivers that commute to and from the office by car every day.

## What is Neon Moves?
Neon Moves is a dance show built on**color, rhythm and emotion**. Professional dancers lead you through a dystopic world shaped by digitalisation and artificial control, which gradually moves towards a stronger sense of humanity. This transformation is expressed through precise choreography and atmospheric lighting, making the visual language part of the story itself. With songs such as**“Toxic”**and **“Yeah!”**, the experience brings instant 2000s recognition, while tracks including **“Crazy in Love”** and**“Can’t Get You Out of My Head”** add more release as the performance develops.

# Powered by 1,800 synchronized LEDs, this high-energy dance show lands in D.C. with 2000s hits like ‘I Gotta Feeling’ and more classics
## Who are THE BLACKOUTS?
THE BLACKOUTS are an **internationally recognised dance collective**known for combining choreography with advanced LED costume technology. Their journey began in Switzerland before appearances on **_Switzerland’s Got Talent, Das Supertalent_** and **_Britain’s Got Talent_** brought their work to wider audiences.
Their performances use around**1,800 individually controllable LEDs**, synchronised down to the millisecond. That precision lets the group create illusions that depend on exact timing. Dancers can emerge from darkness, vanish between beats, or reshape the stage through **rapidly changing formations and patterns of light**, making this light play part of the choreography.

A new study has revealed Melbourne to be Australia’s most congested city with motorists spending close to 100 hours stuck in traffic.
The [Novated Lease Australia](https://www.novatedleaseaustralia.com.au/) study looked at yearly emissions and petrol prices due to congestion, amount of hours per year spent travelling and how many of those are spent in congestion.
Using data sourced from navigation specialist TomTom, the study revealed Melburnians spend on average 205 hours on the road each year.
About 92 of these are spent sitting in heavy traffic and congestion, with residents generally needing about 21 minutes to drive 10km.

# Novated Lease Australia study reveals how long Australians spend in congestion per year with Melbourne coming in first
![Image 7: Melburnians have been revealed to spend about 92 hours in heavy traffic and congestion. Picture: Jason Edwards.](https://content.api.news/v3/images/bin/3e82aa67e13592183c1234bbcbc15b31?width=150)
Melburnians have been revealed to spend about 92 hours in heavy traffic and congestion. Picture: Jason Edwards.
According to the company, congestion costs drivers $205 worth of petrol per year and 247kg of pollution is emitted as motorists creep along in traffic.
Sydney came in second with an annual average of 203 hours spent driving, including 83 hours of congestion – equalling an average of $175 spent on fuel last year due to congestion.
On average however it takes motorists 22 minutes to travel 10km – a little slower than it takes in Melbourne to go the same distance.
![Image 8: Sydney came in second with residents spending about 83 hours per year stuck in congestion and heavy traffic. Picture: Richard Dobson.](https://content.api.news/v3/images/bin/1ecbbd26a4001525faa541ed03b67997?width=150)
Sydney came in second with residents spending about 83 hours per year stuck in congestion and heavy traffic. Picture: Richard Dobson.

# Washington, D.C. Traffic Is Officially The Second Worst Traffic In The Country
## How bad is D.C. traffic?
According to the 2023 TomTom Traffic Index, D.C. traffic is among the slowest in the entire country, ranking at **#2 in the U.S.**behind only NYC. D.C. traffic was rated the **5th worst in all of North America**, and the overall **55th worst in the entire world**. The average travel time per 10 km (equal to just over 6 miles) in D.C. this past year was measured at **21 minutes and 20 seconds**, which happens to be a 10-second increase from the average in 2022. Given how slow it takes to get from place to place in the city, it seems fitting that the average speed during rush hour in D.C. was**14 mph**, which is painfully slow for those trying to get to their destinations on time.
![Image 7: d.c. traffic](https://offloadmedia.feverup.com/secretdc.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/19085624/dc-traffic-2.jpg)
Image via f11photo from Getty Images
To convert the reality of how bad D.C. traffic was in 2023, the**average Washingtonian lost about 86 hours of their time last year just sitting in D.C. traffic** during rush hour. In other words, even if you spent three days straight sitting in your car without ever leaving, you’d still have 14 additional hours to equate to the amount of time that the average D.C. driver spent sitting around in traffic last year!
Additionally, based on the calculations of the Traffic Index, this past year the average one-way commute in D.C. of around 6 miles would result in a yearly total of 205 hours spent driving, over 2,000 lbs of CO2 emissions, and around $418 spent on gas. The most shocking aspect of that average is that it’s also only considering a one-way commute, and considering how commutes are certainly a two-way obligation, you can assume the averages above can be roughly doubled for D.C. drivers that commute to and from the office by car every day.
